statement: There are a function u and a vector field X, smooth on the one-sided manifold Mext, with the following properties. (1) u ≥ |X|g everywhere and u > 0 in Int Mext. For every q′ with 1/2 < q′ < min{q, 1}, (11.3) u = b0 + O2(r−q′ ), X = bi ∂i + O2(r−q′ ). (2) In the interior, sym ∇X = −uK, (11.4) ∆u = − div(K(X, ·)♯ ), (11.5) Hess u = u(Ricg +τK − 2K2 ) − LXK + 8πX(iJj). (11.6) Here (K2)ij = Ki kKkj, and parentheses denote averaged symmetrization. These equations extend smoothly to S. (3) On R × Int Mext the Lorentzian metric (11.7) g = −u2 dt2 + gij( dxi + Xi dt)( dxj + Xj dt) has stationary Killing field ξ = ∂t and induces (g, K) on t = 0, with future normal n = u−1(∂t − X) and the second fundamental form convention K = 1 2Lng. Its Einstein 66 OPENAI tensor satisfies (11.8) uGij = −8πX(iJj), uµ + J(X) = 0. Set N = u2 − |X|2. Then µN = 0, and, throughout this stationary spacetime, (11.9) G = 8πµ u2 ξ♭ ⊗ ξ♭ , Scalg = 0, Ricg(ξ, ·) = 0. In particular, the spacetime is vacuum on {N > 0}. (4) With ν pointing into the exterior, (11.10) X = uν, ∂νu + K(X, ν) = κ, κ = 1 4m on S. For each i = 1, . . . , ℓ, either u > 0 everywhere on Si, or u = 0 everywhere on Si. This alternative is made separately on each component; the constant κ is common to all components.
